spaces.label: Code (Assembled)
spaces.description: The marketplace-assembly TEST SPACE. All THREE of its session-surface sections are INDEPENDENT implementations assembled from the published PARTS: independent-composer (Composer, ComposerTips, the goal/usage surfaces, the capability adapters), independent-thread (Thread, SectionSessionScope, PresenceSurface, OpeningThreadSkeleton) and independent-rail (SessionRail, the rail chrome pieces, and the three assembly hooks that carry the presence/reorder/primary-action judgement). Its switcher, workspace host, dock column and environment card are packs re-exporting the SHIPPED implementations from @fraym/ui (a granted pack external), byte-identical to the built-in Code space by construction. Its top-bar chrome is at PARITY too: `workspace.actions` is ["jobs","refresh","environment","dock","sound"] — the SAME five the built-in Code space declares (`CODE.workspace.actions`, in the Dimension monorepo that mounts this shelf as a submodule — not a path inside this repo), so the dock toggle and every other top-bar control draw here exactly as they do there (parity restored 2026-09-02, closeout PR-3; the earlier `["environment"]`-only bar was a deliberate narrowing that is no longer wanted). The control and the surface stay separate questions (doc 69 §7.1): the dock SURFACE was reachable by intent even while no toggle was drawn, and listing the action adds the toggle without changing that. This space is the owner-directed experiment that pressure-tests the parts decomposition. The acceptance gate is a live structural and behavioral comparison against the built-in Code space on the same session, SCOPED TO THE SESSION SURFACE (rail, thread, composer, workspace host): DOM multiset equality, byte-identical geometry, and a behavior matrix — with fiber provenance proving the pack renders rather than a silent fallback to the built-in.

preview.tagline: The full Code experience, assembled entirely from marketplace parts — pixel-identical to the built-in.
